questions.subject: PRECALCULUS
questions.topic: Building a circle from three points
questions.learningObjective: Select the construction that determines a unique circle through three surveyed points
questions.stem: A civil survey crew must locate the centre of the circular pond that passes through three benchmark posts. Which construction finds it?

options.text: Bisecting only the first chord, since one midpoint alone locates the circle centre
options.misconception: believes a single chord midpoint is the circle centre

options.text: Bisecting two chords and intersecting their perpendicular bisectors at the centre
Drawing the smallest circle that covers the three posts without touching the middle one
options.misconception: confuses a containing circle with a circumscribed one

options.text: Joining each post to the far post and locating where the three chords concur
options.misconception: expects the chords of one circle to be concurrent

questions.explanation: The perpendicular bisectors of two chords meet at the single point equidistant from all three posts. A containing circle merely encloses the outer posts, and chords of a circle never concur.
questions.hint: Two chords, two bisectors, one intersection point.

questions.subject: PRECALCULUS
questions.topic: Building a circle from a diameter
questions.learningObjective: Compute a circle radius from a stated diameter
questions.stem: A flywheel blank has a diameter of 0.46 m. What is the radius of the circle on which the blank will be turned, in metres?
questions.explanation: The radius is half the diameter, so 0.46 m divided by 2 gives 0.23 m. Doubling that figure again returns the original diameter, which confirms the halving was done once.
questions.hint: Radius is half the diameter.

questions.learningObjective: Correct a misread of centre and radius in a circle equation
questions.stem: A pressure vessel cross-section obeys x squared plus y squared minus 6x plus 8y equals 21. The draftspainter reports the centre as 3, 4 with radius 21. What is wrong?

options.text: The radius is 21 because a constant term is never altered when the square is finished
options.misconception: keeps the constant as the radius unchanged

options.text: The centre should be 3, minus 4 because the 8y term comes from a negative coefficient
options.misconception: misreads the sign of the y coefficient when centring

options.text: The equation describes a hyperbola, so a centre and a radius do not apply here
options.misconception: thinks a positive quadratic form must be a hyperbola

options.text: The centre is 3, minus 4 and the radius is the square root of 46, which is not 21

questions.explanation: Completing the square gives (x-3)^2 + (y+4)^2 = 46, so the centre is 3, minus 4 and the radius is the root of 46. The draftspainter ignored the sign of the y term and the moved constants.
questions.hint: Finish the square before reading off the centre.

options.misconception: uses the axis-aligned box instead of the circle

options.text: Whether the trench passes above the highest point of the tank at the centre
options.misconception: compares heights at the centre only

questions.explanation: A line meets a circle exactly when the shortest distance from the centre to the line is at most the radius. Slope and axis-aligned bounds miss the true separation.

questions.subject: PRECALCULUS
questions.learningObjective: Explain why a single contact point makes a line tangent to a circle
questions.stem: A robotic arm must grip a smooth cylindrical drum of radius 0.4 m with a rubber band. Explain why the band should touch the drum at exactly one point and not along a short arc.

answer.exemplar: A band that touches a circle at a single point is a tangent, and at that point the radius is perpendicular to the band. A single contact therefore gives one clean normal force and one clean friction direction, which is what the gripper needs. A band wrapped along an arc would press at many points with different normals, introducing twisting moments and possible snagging on surface irregularities.

questions.explanation: A single contact point means the band is tangent, so the radius there is perpendicular to the band. Wrapping along an arc would add several forces with no unique normal.
questions.hint: Tangent means the radius is perpendicular there.

questions.explanation: Parallel perpendicular bisectors mean the chords are parallel, forcing the three points onto one line. Three collinear points admit no circle, so the survey data must be wrong.
questions.hint: Parallel bisectors signal collinear points.
